cues.en: Hello, everyone. Today, my guest is Dr. Sachin Panda, who is a professor at the Salk Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California, where he studies the body's internal circadian clock, what regulates their circadian clock, and in turn, how this affects a wide variety of processes, including our metabolism, our sleeping patterns, and how active we are, and so much more.
cues.zh: 大家好。今天我请到的嘉宾是 Sachin Panda 博士，他是加州拉霍亚 Salk 生物研究所的教授，主要研究人体内部的昼夜节律生物钟、调节生物钟的因素，以及生物钟如何影响各种生理过程，包括新陈代谢、睡眠模式、身体活动水平等等。

cues.en: Sachin, considering that every single living organism on the planet Earth has this internal biological clock, the circadian clock, can you explain to people who've never heard what a circadian clock is, what it is, and why it's so important? Yeah, so all lives on this planet evolved under a rotating earth. So that means for 12 hours, approximately 12 hours, they had access to light. And for another 12 hours, they were in darkness.
cues.zh: Sachin，考虑到地球上所有生物都有自己的内部生物钟，也就是昼夜节律生物钟，你能否向从未听说过这个概念的人解释一下，什么是昼夜节律生物钟，以及它为什么如此重要？当然。地球上所有生命都是在地球自转的环境中进化而来的。这意味着，大约有12个小时，它们能够接触到光照；而另外12个小时，它们则处于黑暗之中。

cues.en: So that environment, that changing environment, put a tremendous pressure for them to come up with a timing mechanism so that they can anticipate when it's going to be evening or when it's going to be morning so that they can time their activity and sleep accordingly. So that's why almost every organism on this planet have this internal clock that help them anticipate time. And why this is important is if you think about a diurnal
cues.zh: 这种不断变化的环境给生物带来了巨大的生存压力，促使它们发展出一种计时机制，以便提前预判夜晚或早晨何时到来，从而合理安排活动和睡眠。因此，地球上几乎所有生物都有自己的内部生物钟，帮助它们预判时间。至于为什么这很重要，我们可以想想一种昼行性

cues.en: organism, an animal that's active during the daytime. The animal has to anticipate when evening is going to come so that he can rush back to the cave or somewhere, some hiding place. So similarly, just before the dawn, this animal has to wake up before even light hits and then go out and get the first grub. So that's why there is this tremendous pressure to have this biological clock or internal timing.
cues.zh: 生物，也就是白天活动的动物。它必须提前预判夜晚何时到来，这样才能赶在天黑前跑回洞穴，或者其他藏身之处。同样，在黎明到来之前，这种动物就必须醒来，甚至要赶在阳光照射到它之前起床，然后外出寻找第一顿食物。这就是为什么生物需要昼夜节律生物钟，也就是这种内部计时机制。

cues.en: to essentially anticipate what's going to happen. So for most people, we know when we go to bed, maybe after six to eight hours, we wake up. So our clock actually tells us, yes, it's going to be morning. Get up now. So similarly, almost every part of our body has clocks that help us to anticipate when the food is going to come or when we are supposed to run or when you are supposed to take rest. So what we are learning is almost every
cues.zh: 本质上就是预测将要发生什么。对大多数人来说，我们知道上床睡觉后，大概六到八小时会醒来。所以我们的生物钟其实会告诉我们：对，天要亮了，现在起床。同样，我们身体几乎每个部分都有钟，帮我们预测食物什么时候来、什么时候该跑动、什么时候该休息。所以我们了解到的是，几乎每个

cues.en: organ in our body has a clock and it helps this organ to be at peak performance, peak activity at certain time of the day, and then to rest and rejuvenate at the other time of the day. So is this internal biological clock, the circadian clock, it's not something that we're just immediately born with, right? It's not something that just... Yeah, so when you are born, we kind of...
cues.zh: 器官都有钟，帮助这个器官在一天中的某个时间达到最佳表现、最活跃，然后在另一个时间休息和恢复。那么，这个内在的生物钟——昼夜节律钟——并不是我们一出生就立刻具备的，对吧？它不是那种……对，所以当你出生时，我们有点……

cues.zh: 所以婴儿出生时，其实没有这种每天24小时的节律，也没有相应的活动或睡眠。他们不会一睡就是六七个小时。所以我们推测，虽然他们有钟，但这些钟没有彼此连接起来。同时，婴儿也需要大量食物，因为那是他们的生长阶段。所以在最初大概四到六个月里，婴儿

cues.en: Many parents may not notice because we now live in a very artificial environment, but that's the time when there is a clock, but it's not tied to outside light and dark cycle. If you remove that brain part,

cues.en: in a hamster, then this hamster will not have any sense of time, will go to sleep at random time and will wake up after two or three hours and will continue. But what is most exciting is if we take a CN from another hamster and transplant, it's like a brain transplant experiment, then this hamster will get all the rhythms back. That's the earliest example of
cues.zh: 在仓鼠身上，那么这只仓鼠就没有任何时间感，会在随机时间入睡，两三个小时后醒来，然后继续这样。但最令人兴奋的是，如果我们从另一只仓鼠身上取一个SCN并移植过去，这就像脑移植实验，那么这只仓鼠会恢复所有节律。那是最早的例子，

cues.en: neural transplant transferring behavior from one animal to another animal. And just imagine only when we are awake we eat or we exercise. So that's why all other organs, organs related to eating, for example, our gut, our liver,
cues.zh: 神经移植将行为从一只动物转移到另一只动物。这基本上确立了这个脑区就是作为主昼夜振荡器或昼夜时钟的部分，因为它 orchestrates 这个每日节律以及醒来和入睡。想象一下，只有我们醒着时才进食或锻炼。所以这就是为什么所有其他器官，比如与进食相关的器官，我们的肠道、肝脏，

So that's why this master clock is so much important for our health.

cues.zh: 但如果你改变它们的光暗周期，它们会在六到七天内重新调整。它们重新调整的方式和视力正常的小鼠完全一样。所以这在视觉科学里算是一个75年未解的问题。眼睛里这个额外的光受体是什么？我们知道它在眼睛里，因为很多上战场因枪伤失去双眼的人，还有

cues.en: Yes. So, you kind of are changing gears here, and I think it's very important to point out for people that aren't familiar with this. So, we've been talking for some time about this master regulator clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus region of the brain, and how light is what sets that clock, what regulates that clock. And in turn, those are regulating...
cues.zh: 是的。所以，你在这里有点转换话题了，我认为向不熟悉这一机制的人指出这一点非常重要。因此，我们讨论这个位于大脑视交叉上核区域的主调节钟已经有一段时间了，以及光是如何设定这个生物钟、调节这个生物钟的。反过来，它们又在调节……

cues.en: a wide variety of different physiological processes. But then you just mentioned something very important, and that is that in addition to that clock, there are other clocks, for example, in our liver, in our muscle, in our heart, that also are regulated. But your research, and maybe we can start to talk about this, they seem to be regulated by something different, by when you eat, by when you take in food. And I know for myself, I've always, I've known
cues.zh: 各种各样不同的生理过程。但你刚刚提到了非常重要的一点，那就是除了那个生物钟之外，还有其他生物钟，例如在我们肝脏、肌肉、心脏中的生物钟，它们也会受到调节。但你的研究——也许我们可以开始讨论这个——它们似乎受别的东西调节，即你何时进食、何时摄入食物。我知道就我个人而言，我一直以来都知道

cues.en: about the circadian clocks in the liver and how they regulate metabolism. I know that we're most insulin sensitive during the early morning hours and most insulin insensitive in the evening. And so I've always tried to not eat too late because I'm like, well, I don't want to eat this in a high carbohydrate meal when I'm the most insulin insensitive. It doesn't make any sense. It's much easier for me to do that in the winter months when it's...
cues.zh: 关于肝脏中的生物钟以及它们如何调节新陈代谢的知识。我知道我们在清晨对胰岛素最敏感，而在晚上对胰岛素最不敏感。所以我总是尽量不要吃得太晚，因为我想，嗯，我可不想在对胰岛素最不敏感的时候吃高碳水化合物的一餐。这毫无意义。对我来说，在冬天的时候，这样做要容易得多，因为……

cues.en: gets dark earlier, I find it more difficult when spring and summer occur because it's lighter out, I'm working later, and therefore I eat later. So let's talk a little bit about how food regulates these clocks and these different tissues. Yes, a few years ago, we started looking at which genes are regulated by clock in different organs. So if we look at liver, there might be
cues.zh: 天变短了，我发现春夏时节更难熬，因为天亮得更久，我工作得更晚，因此吃得更晚。所以让我们谈谈食物如何调节这些时钟和不同组织。是的，几年前我们开始研究不同器官中哪些基因受时钟调控。所以看肝脏，可能有

cues.en: there are somewhere between 3,000 to 5,000 genes that turn on at a certain time of the day or night. And so that's a lot of genes. That's almost 30% of expressed genome or whatever. But what is interesting is we said, well, we did a very simple experiment where these are done in mice. So the mice, night eating mice, mice usually eat during the nighttime.
cues.zh: 大约有3000到5000个基因在一天中或夜晚的特定时间开启。这是很多基因，几乎占表达基因组30%左右。但有趣的是，我们做了一个非常简单的实验，是在小鼠身上做的。小鼠是夜间进食的，通常夜间吃东西。

cues.en: Then we asked, well, there is a master regulator in the brain that's telling the rest of the body when the timing is, when it's day or night. And let's give mice food in the middle of the day, just like the shift workers work in the nighttime, they eat. If we do that, then what happens to the liver? All liver genes that cycle, they take the cue from light-dark cycle or from the food. Because we have these two groups of mice.
cues.zh: 然后我们问，大脑里有个主调节器告诉身体其他部分何时是白天或夜晚。让我们在白天给小鼠喂食，就像轮班工人夜间工作、夜间进食。如果这样做，肝脏会怎样？所有循环的肝脏基因会从光暗周期或食物中获取信号。因为我们有两组小鼠。

cues.en: Both groups of mice are in the same light-dark cycle. One group eats during day, one group eats during night. If the liver takes cue from light-dark cycle, then all cyclings in should be identical in two groups. If the liver clocks take cue from eating time, then the day-fed animals will have a different clock than the night-fed animals. And that's exactly what we found, that even though the light-dark cycle was the same for both animals.
cues.zh: 两组小鼠处于相同的光暗周期。一组白天进食，一组夜间进食。如果肝脏从光暗周期获取信号，那么两组的所有循环应该相同。如果肝脏时钟从进食时间获取信号，那么白天喂养的动物时钟将与夜间喂养的不同。这正是我们发现的，尽管两组动物的光暗周期相同。

cues.en: the liver clock responds to when the mice ate. So the day fed animals had the same 3,000 genes cycling. The night fed animals had the same 3,000 gene cycling. But now the genes that were turning on during daytime in the day fed animals, now they turn on at nighttime in the night fed animal. So that means the time when we eat tells our liver clock when to turn on the genes and when to turn up.
cues.zh: 肝脏时钟会响应小鼠进食的时间。所以白天进食的动物，同样的3000个基因在循环。夜间进食的动物，同样的3000个基因也在循环。但白天进食动物中白天开启的基因，现在在夜间进食动物中变成了夜间开启。这意味着我们进食的时间告诉肝脏时钟何时开启基因、何时上调表达。

cues.en: the light has very little impact. We cannot say no impact, very little impact on these cycling genes in liver. So that experiment has been replicated now and what we are learning is almost every organ in our periphery outside the brain kind of follows when we eat. So then what becomes very important in the daily life is the first sight of bright light and the first bite of food.
cues.zh: 光照的影响非常小。不能说没有影响，但对肝脏中这些循环基因的影响非常小。这个实验现在已经被重复验证，我们了解到的是，大脑之外几乎每个外周器官都在一定程度上跟随我们的进食时间。所以在日常生活中，非常重要的就是第一眼看到强光和第一口进食。

cues.en: those two determine how our body clocks work. So now we are working on how this timing of eating or timing of light affects our health in general. And you have a certain term, I guess, I don't know who coined the phrase, but it's called time restricted feeding. Yeah. And you've done, there's been experiments that you've done in these mice where you've fed them various
cues.zh: 这两者决定了我们生物钟的运作方式。现在我们正在研究进食时间或光照时间如何总体影响我们的健康。有一个术语，我不知道是谁提出的，叫做限时进食。是的。你做过实验，在这些小鼠身上喂食各种

cues.en: types of food, high fat diet, high sugar diet, normal chow diet, and you've restricted their time feeding during the night, the mouse day hours, which is actually the night because they're nocturnal. And you found some very interesting things. So can you talk a little bit about those findings? So what we have seen is when we, in experimental animals, if they don't have a clock,
cues.zh: 不同类型的食物，高脂饮食、高糖饮食、正常饲料，并且你限制了它们在夜间——也就是小鼠的白天时段，实际上对它们来说是夜晚，因为它们是夜行动物——的进食时间。你发现了一些非常有趣的现象。能谈谈这些发现吗？我们观察到的是，在实验动物中，如果它们没有时钟，

cues.en: then the metabolism goes really weird. So just like I said, a metabolism works like this traffic signal in downtown. And if they're not timed properly, then there'll be disease. Similarly, for a very long time, we knew in the field that mice that don't have circadian clock because they lack a gene or have a mutation.
cues.zh: 那么代谢就会变得非常异常。就像我说的，代谢就像市中心的交通信号灯。如果时间不对，就会生病。同样，很长一段时间以来，我们在该领域就知道，缺乏某个基因或带有突变的小鼠没有生物钟。

cues.en: They have various metabolic defects. They have obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, et cetera. We also know people who do shift work for a very long period of time, they are also highly likely to get metabolic disease, cancer, accelerated aging. So there is this idea that clocks are important. If we don't have a good functioning clock, then that's bad for us. Then we went back and asked, OK, normal circumstances.
cues.zh: 它们有多种代谢缺陷，包括肥胖、糖尿病、心血管疾病等等。我们还知道，长期倒班工作的人也很容易患上代谢疾病、癌症，并加速衰老。所以有一种观点认为，生物钟很重要。如果我们的生物钟功能不佳，那对我们是不利的。然后我们回过头来问，好吧，正常情况下。

cues.en: What are the conditions that can actually break down our clock? And what we found was when mice are given high-fat diet or any unhealthy food, then the food itself breaks down their clock. So they actually don't have a good eating fasting rhythm. So the mice eat throughout day and night.
cues.zh: 哪些条件会真正破坏我们的生物钟？我们发现，当给小鼠喂食高脂饮食或任何不健康食物时，食物本身就会破坏它们的生物钟。所以它们实际上没有良好的进食-禁食节律。结果小鼠昼夜不停地进食。

cues.en: We knew that high-fat diet and high fructose diet, high fructose diet, all of these diets that are used experimentally in laboratory conditions give rise to all these diseases. And people always thought it's what and how much the mice ate that determine the disease. But what we found is, well, these mice are also not eating at the same time. So maybe when they eat also matters. So we did a very simple experiment where
cues.zh: 我们知道高脂饮食和高果糖饮食，高果糖饮食，所有这些在实验室条件下用于实验的饮食都会引发这些疾病。人们一直认为，决定疾病的是小鼠吃了什么以及吃了多少。但我们发现，这些小鼠进食的时间也不一致。所以也许它们什么时候吃也很重要。于是我们做了一个非常简单的实验，其中

cues.en: We took two groups of mice, completely identical set of mice. No genes were changed. No drugs were given. And one group of mice ate whatever they wanted to eat. And to begin with, we gave them a high fat diet. So they're getting somewhere between 45% to 60% of their food from fat, calories from fat. So that means it will be equivalent to
cues.zh: 我们取了两组小鼠，完全相同的一组小鼠。没有改变基因。没有给药。一组小鼠想吃什么就吃什么。一开始，我们给它们高脂饮食。所以它们从脂肪中获取的热量大约占45%到60%。这意味着这相当于

cues.en: humans eating all of their food from cheese, nachos, ice cream, or Western diet. So they're getting fat and sugar. So they're getting fat and sugar, all this stuff. And then the other group got the same number of calories and the same type of food, exactly identical food. But they had to eat all their food within eight to 12 hours in nighttime. So in some experiments, we have done eight hours, nine hours, 10 hours, 12 hours, like that.
cues.zh: 人类所有食物都来自奶酪、玉米片、冰淇淋或西方饮食。所以它们摄入脂肪和糖。它们摄入脂肪和糖，所有这些。然后另一组摄入相同数量的热量和相同类型的食物，完全相同的食物。但它们必须在夜间8到12小时内吃完所有食物。所以在一些实验中，我们做了8小时、9小时、10小时、12小时，诸如此类。

cues.en: And the most surprising thing is, means this is something that everybody, a lot of laboratories around the world do. There are 11,000 papers showing high-fat diet causes obesity. And we said, okay, so now we control for time. So since time was restricted, calorie was not restricted, so that's why you call it time-restricted feeding.
cues.zh: 最令人惊讶的是，这是全世界很多实验室都在做的事。有11000篇论文表明高脂饮食会导致肥胖。我们说，好，那现在我们来控制时间。因为时间受限，热量不受限，所以称之为限时进食。

cues.en: And surprisingly, the mice that ate for eight to 12 hours, they did not become obese, diabetic, and they had a normal liver function, and they had normal cholesterol, et cetera. And then in the next set of experiments, we expose these mice to high fructose diet, high carb diet, high sucrose diet, all kinds of diets, either ad libitum, whenever they can eat, or they have to eat within eight to 12 hours. And in most cases, we see
cues.zh: 出乎意料的是，那些在8到12小时内进食的小鼠并没有变得肥胖、患糖尿病，它们的肝功能正常，胆固醇也正常，等等。然后在下一组实验中，我们让这些小鼠接触高果糖饮食、高碳水饮食、高蔗糖饮食，各种饮食，要么随意进食，想吃就吃，要么必须在8到12小时内吃完。在大多数情况下，我们看到

cues.en: the time restricted feeding has huge beneficial impact. Even when mice eat standard diet, normal chow, which is supposed to be very healthy, and mice actually eat most of their food, nearly 70% of food during nighttime. They eat a little bit during daytime. But if they completely restrict that to eight to 12 hours, then the muscle mass goes up, the fat mass decreases, and they're more coordinated. So if you put them on a rotating drum, then they're coordinate on the rotating drum for a long time.
cues.zh: 限时进食有巨大的有益影响。即使小鼠吃标准饮食、普通鼠粮，本应非常健康，而小鼠实际上大部分食物，近70%是在夜间吃的。白天吃得很少。但如果完全限制在8到12小时内，那么肌肉量上升，脂肪量下降，而且它们更协调。所以如果把它们放在旋转鼓上，它们能在旋转鼓上长时间保持协调。

cues.en: So the bottom line is this time, so in these experiments where we kept what and how much they had constant, the only thing that we changed is when they ate, then we see this huge beneficial impact. And that correlates with very robust clock in the liver and in other metabolic organs. And why this is important is two things. One is many of us have really...
cues.zh: 所以底线是，在这些实验中，我们保持吃什么和吃多少不变，唯一改变的是它们什么时候吃，然后我们就看到了巨大的有益影响。这与肝脏和其他代谢器官中非常稳健的生物钟相关。为什么这很重要，有两点。一是我们很多人真的……

cues.en: I won't say bad, but we don't have much control over what and how much food we eat. As soon as we get out of our home, all the food we eat outside, we have very little control over it. So the only control we have actually is on our time. So that's why we think this can be a good entry point to a better living by controlling time.
cues.zh: 我不会说不好，但我们对吃什么、吃多少其实控制力有限。一旦出门，外面吃的所有东西，我们几乎都很难掌控。所以实际上我们唯一能控制的就是时间。正因如此，我们认为通过控制时间，可以成为改善生活的一个良好切入点。

cues.en: The second thing is, it also doesn't take away this idea that nutrition doesn't matter, the quality doesn't matter, because even in our high fat-fed mice, we don't see they completely become normal, just like the normal child-fed mice. They're much healthier. So to have better health, you still have to change what and how much you eat, but timing becomes much easier to manage.
cues.zh: 第二点是，这也没有否定营养不重要、质量不重要的观点，因为即便在我们的高脂喂养小鼠中，我们也没看到它们完全变得和正常喂养的小鼠一样。它们要健康得多。所以要想更健康，你仍然需要改变吃什么、吃多少，但时间安排变得容易管理多了。

cues.en: So, you just covered so much. This experiment that you did right here, this publication, even before you've gone on to some small human studies, but this convinced me to do a time-restricted feeding schedule because, well, for a couple of reasons. So, just to reiterate, these mice that were fed a high-fat diet
cues.zh: 你刚才讲了很多。你在这里做的这个实验、这篇论文，甚至在你还没开展一些小规模人体研究之前，就已经说服我采用限时进食的方案了，原因有几个。再重申一下，这些被喂食高脂饮食的小鼠

cues.en: They fed the same amount of calories, but those that ate during their waking hours, or my sexual night, within, I think it was 12 hours, they had 70% less fat mass. Yeah, so they had 28% less body mass total.
cues.zh: 它们摄入相同数量的卡路里，但在清醒时段进食的——也就是我所说的夜间时段，在大概12小时内——它们脂肪量减少了70%。是的，所以它们的总体重减少了28%。

cues.en: change in body mass is mostly due to fat because they have 70% less fat. That's amazing. Right there. They're eating the same crappy food, but they're eating it when their liver can process it the best, when they're able to regulate their blood sugar, when they're able to oxidize fats, things like that. So that was really cool. And then the second thing was...
cues.zh: 体重的变化主要来自脂肪，因为它们的脂肪减少了70%。太惊人了。就在那里。它们吃的是同样糟糕的食物，但吃的时间是肝脏最能处理的时候，是它们能调节血糖、能氧化脂肪的时候，诸如此类。所以这真的很酷。然后第二点是……

cues.en: I eat a very, very, very health conscientious. I try to get a wide variety of vegetables and fruits and good fats and all that stuff, omega-3s. But I'm always trying to find the low-hanging fruit to sort of delay the aging process in a way or become as optimal as I possibly can. So the mice that were fed a normal chow diet, high in fiber and all these things, vitamins.
cues.zh: 我平时饮食非常、非常注重健康。我尽量摄入各种蔬菜、水果、优质脂肪等等，比如 omega-3。但我总想找些最容易入手的方法来延缓衰老，或者把身体调整到最佳状态。话说回来，那些喂食普通饲料的小鼠，饲料里富含纤维、维生素等各种营养。

cues.en: You said they actually had more lean muscle mass. Yeah, that is very interesting because for me It's much easier to lose fat than it is to gain muscle It's difficult to gain muscle and as you age it becomes even more so yeah, and muscle mass is very important It protects you from frailty things like that. So any ideas as to how Just restricting your and but we should probably talk about what starts that clock. Yeah, what what
cues.zh: 你说它们的瘦肌肉量其实反而更多。对，这非常有意思，因为对我来说，减脂可比增肌容易多了。增肌本来就难，上了年纪之后更是如此，而肌肉量又极其重要，能避免身体衰弱。所以关于仅仅限制进食……不过我们可能得先聊聊究竟是什么启动了那个计时钟。对，到底什么算……

cues.en: food, it doesn't necessarily have to be a calorie, right? It can be black coffee or something like that. But anyways, any ideas as to what is allowing you to keep on more muscle mass? Yeah, so that actually is a big mystery because in the first series of experiments, we are essentially reporting observations, what happens. The reason why we looked into muscle mass is
cues.zh: 食物，它不一定非得含有热量，对吧？黑咖啡之类的算吗？但不管怎么说，关于为什么能保留更多肌肉量，目前有什么线索吗？是的，这其实是个很大的谜团，因为在第一阶段的实验中，我们本质上只是在记录观察到的现象。我们之所以去测量肌肉量，是因为……

cues.en: Initially, we thought that these mice, when they're going through such a prolonged period of fasting, in some experiments, they're going for 12 to 16 hours of fasting every day. And many people think that when you go through this prolonged fasting, you lose your muscle because muscle, the protein gets used to make glucose. That's why you measure lean mass. And surprisingly, we found that the lean mass actually increased.
cues.zh: 最初我们以为，这些小鼠经历这么长时间的断食——在某些实验中它们每天要断食 12 到 16 个小时。很多人都认为长时间断食会掉肌肉，因为肌肉蛋白会被用来转化成葡萄糖。所以我们才去测了瘦体重。令人惊讶的是，我们发现它们的瘦体重居然还增加了。

cues.en: Whereas the fat mass decreased, that was a big surprise. That's what we reported. But we haven't looked at exactly why the muscle mass increases. But what we are seeing recently is there are some correlation. Other people have published recently that nicotinamide riboside. This is a precursor for NAD. If that is given to mice, they also gain muscle mass or they maintain their muscle mass.
cues.zh: 而脂肪量减少了，这非常令人惊讶。这就是我们报告的结果。但我们还没有确切研究为什么肌肉量会增加。不过我们最近看到了一些相关性。其他人最近发表了关于烟酰胺核糖的研究。这是NAD的前体。如果给小鼠服用，它们也会增加肌肉量或维持肌肉量。

cues.en: And this nicotinamide riboside is converted to energy and increased amount of energy is always better for any cell because that is the precursor to the energy currency of the cell, that's ATP. And what we are seeing is in many of our mouse experiment, we see the energy level actually goes off slightly.
cues.zh: 这种烟酰胺核糖被转化为能量，能量增加对任何细胞总是更好，因为它是细胞能量货币ATP的前体。我们在许多小鼠实验中看到，能量水平实际上略有上升。

cues.en: So, this is a natural way to boost up energy level, not only in muscle in almost every organ. So, I think that might be one of the many different reasons why we're gaining muscle mass. But we can't explain with the current data why they gain muscle mass. Can I ask you another question? Sure.
